title: The Religion of Speed

content_html:
29 May, 2026

At some point, “moving fast” stopped being a practical concern and became a moral position. You see it damn near everywhere now.

How fast can we ship this? How fast can we respond? How fast can we hire? How fast can we scale? How fast can we pivot? How fast can we get something, anything, in front of people so we can say we’re making progress?

It’s treated like proof of seriousness. If you’re moving fast, you’re ambitious. If you’re cautious, you’re scared. If you ask to slow down and think, you’re blocking momentum. If you point out that the current plan has all the structural integrity of wet cardboard, you’re being negative.

This is how a lot of bad work gets protected.

Not because it’s good, useful, or even halfway thought through, but because it’s fast. Speed has become a kind of institutional narcotic.

It gives people the feeling of motion without requiring the discipline of judgment.

“Do not confuse motion and progress. A rocking horse keeps moving but does not make any progress.”

— Alfred A. Montapert

Everyone gets to feel busy. Everyone gets to feel urgent. Everyone gets to point at the smoke coming off the machine and say, “See? We’re doing something.” The problem is that a lot of what gets called speed is just impatience with a different name.

Real speed exists. Real speed is what happens when the work is understood, the constraints are clear, the people involved know what they’re doing, and the decisions have been made cleanly enough that execution can happen without constant re-litigation.

That kind of speed is rare. Most speed is vague requirements, half-decisions, unexamined dependencies, missing context, and a room full of people quietly hoping the next person in the chain figures out what was never actually decided. Then, when the thing breaks, everyone acts surprised.

Of course it broke. It was built under the assumption that thinking was the expensive part.

This shows up constantly in the software industry, but software is often just the place where the wreckage becomes visible to most people.

The same thing happens in operations, management, hiring, logistics, customer service, product development, and damn near everything else where people mistake activity for progress.

People rush through the part where understanding is supposed to happen, then spend ten times longer cleaning up the consequences. The original rushed work gets recorded as “fast.” The cleanup gets recorded as “unexpected.” The rework gets recorded as “iteration.” The confusion gets recorded as “alignment.” The preventable failure gets recorded as “learning.”

This is how organizations end up with systems nobody trusts, processes nobody understands, meetings nobody wants, dashboards nobody believes, and workarounds that become load-bearing pieces of the business.

Nobody set out to build that. They just kept choosing speed over comprehension, one small decision at a time, until the whole place became a series of monuments to things resembling productivity but having no actual productive worth. Then some poor bastard gets hired to “modernize” it, which usually means replacing the visible mess while leaving the original religion intact.

The funny part is that slowing down usually does not mean moving slowly. That’s the part people miss.

Slowing down means refusing to skip the part where the work becomes legible. What are we actually trying to produce? Who depends on it? What breaks if this assumption is wrong? What do we already know? What are we pretending not to know? Where has this failed before? What has to be true for this to work?

Boring, load-bearing questions that keep our work from turning into Waco. But those questions feel slow because they remove the little dopamine hit people get from motion.

You can’t posture your way through them. You can’t hide inside urgency. You can’t turn the conversation into a PowerPoint deck and call it progress.

You have to actually understand the work, which is the part a lot of people are trying to avoid.

Speed is attractive because it lets people stay slightly abstract. It lets them keep decisions fuzzy. It lets them avoid responsibility for details until those details become someone else’s emergency.

And when the emergency arrives, speed becomes the answer again. Move faster. Fix faster. Hire faster. Replace faster. Ship faster. The same disease silently becomes the cure.

There is a difference between urgency and haste. Urgency is appropriate when something matters and time is real. Haste is what happens when people want the emotional relief of action without the burden of clarity.

"Make haste slowly."

— Baltasar Gracián

The older I get, the less impressed I am by speed as a standalone virtue. I care whether the work holds up. I care whether the person doing it understands the shape of the problem. I care whether the decision survives contact with reality. I care whether we are creating fewer problems than we solve.

That doesn’t require theatrical slowness.

Nobody needs to sit around writing their own deployment infra for six months to prove they’re thoughtful. This isn’t an argument for dragging your feet or turning every decision into an excuse for yet-another-meeting. It’s an argument for respecting the work enough to do it properly the first time.

Understand first, decide second, and only when you've done the proper due diligence, then you can/should move.

When those steps get reversed, the bill always comes due. Sometimes the bill is a broken system. Sometimes it’s a burned-out team. Sometimes it’s a customer who quietly leaves. Sometimes it’s years of operational scar tissue that everyone works around because nobody has the patience to go back and understand what actually happened.

The Religion of Speed survives because it gives people a clean excuse. It lets them say the world is changing too fast, the market is too competitive, the customer is too demanding, the team is too small, the budget is too tight, and the window is closing...blah blah blah.

Sometimes those things are true. Often, they are just cover for the fact that nobody wants to do the slower, harder work of making sense before moving.

The better work is usually calmer than people expect. It still moves. It still ships. It still makes decisions. But it does not confuse panic with seriousness. It does not treat every pause as weakness. It does not worship motion for its own sake. It accepts the deeply unfashionable idea that some things get faster only after you stop rushing them.

That is the part the speed cult never seems to understand.

You can move fast for a while by skipping thought, skipping clarity, skipping context, and skipping responsibility. But the work remembers. The system remembers. The people stuck maintaining it remember.

Eventually, reality collects what it's due. And reality is very patient.

sentences.zh: 当人们希望采取行动来缓解情绪，而又不想承担清晰的负担时，就会出现匆忙的情况。

sentences.zh: “慢慢来。” — 巴尔塔萨尔·葛拉西安

sentences.en: "Make haste slowly."
sentences.zh: “慢慢来。”

blocks.html_en: The older I get, the less impressed I am by speed as a standalone virtue. I care whether the work holds up. I care whether the person doing it understands the shape of the problem. I care whether the decision survives contact with reality. I care whether we are creating fewer problems than we solve.

sentences.en: The older I get, the less impressed I am by speed as a standalone virtue.
sentences.zh: 随着年龄的增长，我对速度这一独立美德的印象就越淡薄。

sentences.en: I care whether the work holds up.
sentences.zh: 我关心工作是否能坚持下去。

sentences.en: I care whether the person doing it understands the shape of the problem.
sentences.zh: 我关心做这件事的人是否理解问题的本质。

sentences.en: I care whether the decision survives contact with reality.
sentences.zh: 我关心这个决定是否能经受住现实的考验。

sentences.en: I care whether we are creating fewer problems than we solve.
sentences.zh: 我关心的是我们制造的问题是否少于我们解决的问题。

blocks.html_en: That doesn’t require theatrical slowness.

sentences.en: That doesn’t require theatrical slowness.
sentences.zh: 这并不需要戏剧般的缓慢。

blocks.html_en: Nobody needs to sit around writing their own deployment infra for six months to prove they’re thoughtful. This isn’t an argument for dragging your feet or turning every decision into an excuse for yet-another-meeting. It’s an argument for respecting the work enough to do it properly the first time.

sentences.en: Nobody needs to sit around writing their own deployment infra for six months to prove they’re thoughtful.
sentences.zh: 没有人需要花费六个月的时间来编写自己的部署基础设施来证明他们是深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: This isn’t an argument for dragging your feet or turning every decision into an excuse for yet-another-meeting.
sentences.zh: 这并不是要拖延或将每一个决定变成再次会议的借口。

sentences.en: It’s an argument for respecting the work enough to do it properly the first time.
sentences.zh: 这是对工作的充分尊重，第一次就做好的论点。

blocks.html_en: Understand first, decide second, and only when you've done the proper due diligence, then you can/should move.

sentences.en: Understand first, decide second, and only when you've done the proper due diligence, then you can/should move.
sentences.zh: 首先了解，其次决定，只有当你完成了适当的尽职调查后，你才可以/应该搬家。

blocks.html_en: When those steps get reversed, the bill always comes due. Sometimes the bill is a broken system. Sometimes it’s a burned-out team. Sometimes it’s a customer who quietly leaves. Sometimes it’s years of operational scar tissue that everyone works around because nobody has the patience to go back and understand what actually happened.

sentences.en: When those steps get reversed, the bill always comes due.
sentences.zh: 当这些步骤颠倒过来时，账单总会到期。

sentences.en: Sometimes the bill is a broken system.
sentences.zh: 有时账单是一个损坏的系统。

sentences.en: Sometimes it’s a burned-out team.
sentences.zh: 有时这是一支精疲力竭的团队。

sentences.en: Sometimes it’s a customer who quietly leaves.
sentences.zh: 有时是顾客悄悄离开。

sentences.en: Sometimes it’s years of operational scar tissue that everyone works around because nobody has the patience to go back and understand what actually happened.
sentences.zh: 有时，每个人都在努力解决多年的手术疤痕组织，因为没有人有耐心回去了解到底发生了什么。

blocks.html_en: The Religion of Speed survives because it gives people a clean excuse. It lets them say the world is changing too fast, the market is too competitive, the customer is too demanding, the team is too small, the budget is too tight, and the window is closing...blah blah blah.

sentences.en: The Religion of Speed survives because it gives people a clean excuse.
sentences.zh: 速度宗教得以幸存，是因为它给了人们一个干净的借口。

sentences.en: It lets them say the world is changing too fast, the market is too competitive, the customer is too demanding, the team is too small, the budget is too tight, and the window is closing...blah blah blah.
sentences.zh: 这让他们说世界变化太快、市场竞争太激烈、客户要求太高、团队太小、预算太紧张、窗口即将关闭……等等等等。

blocks.html_en: Sometimes those things are true. Often, they are just cover for the fact that nobody wants to do the slower, harder work of making sense before moving.

sentences.en: Sometimes those things are true.
sentences.zh: 有时这些事情是真的。

sentences.en: Often, they are just cover for the fact that nobody wants to do the slower, harder work of making sense before moving.
sentences.zh: 通常，它们只是为了掩盖这样一个事实：没有人愿意在搬家之前做更慢、更艰苦的工作来理解情况。

blocks.html_en: The better work is usually calmer than people expect. It still moves. It still ships. It still makes decisions. But it does not confuse panic with seriousness. It does not treat every pause as weakness. It does not worship motion for its own sake. It accepts the deeply unfashionable idea that some things get faster only after you stop rushing them.

sentences.en: The better work is usually calmer than people expect.
sentences.zh: 更好的工作通常比人们想象的更平静。

sentences.en: It still moves.
sentences.zh: 它仍然在移动。

sentences.en: It still ships.
sentences.zh: 它仍然发货。

sentences.en: It still makes decisions.
sentences.zh: 它仍然做出决定。

sentences.en: But it does not confuse panic with seriousness.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有将恐慌与严重性混为一谈。

sentences.en: It does not treat every pause as weakness.
sentences.zh: 它并不把每一次停顿都视为弱点。

sentences.en: It does not worship motion for its own sake.
sentences.zh: 它并不是为了运动本身而崇拜运动。

sentences.en: It accepts the deeply unfashionable idea that some things get faster only after you stop rushing them.
sentences.zh: 它接受了一种非常不流行的想法，即有些事情只有在你停止催促之后才会变得更快。

blocks.html_en: That is the part the speed cult never seems to understand.

sentences.en: That is the part the speed cult never seems to understand.
sentences.zh: 这就是速度崇拜者似乎永远无法理解的部分。

blocks.html_en: You can move fast for a while by skipping thought, skipping clarity, skipping context, and skipping responsibility. But the work remembers. The system remembers. The people stuck maintaining it remember.

sentences.en: You can move fast for a while by skipping thought, skipping clarity, skipping context, and skipping responsibility.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过跳过思考、跳过清晰、跳过上下文和跳过责任来快速行动一段时间。

sentences.en: But the work remembers.
sentences.zh: 但作品会记住。

sentences.en: The system remembers.
sentences.zh: 系统记住了。

sentences.en: The people stuck maintaining it remember.
sentences.zh: 人们坚持维护它记住了。

blocks.html_en: Eventually, reality collects what it's due. And reality is very patient.

sentences.en: Eventually, reality collects what it's due.
sentences.zh: 最终，现实会带来它应得的。

sentences.en: And reality is very patient.
sentences.zh: 而现实是非常有耐心的。

content_html_zh:
29 May, 2026

在某种程度上，“快速行动”不再是一个实际问题，而是成为一种道德立场。 现在你几乎到处都能看到它。

我们能多快运送这个？ 我们能多快做出反应？ 我们能多快招聘？ 我们能以多快的速度扩展？ 我们能以多快的速度转向？ 我们能以多快的速度把某样东西、任何东西呈现在人们面前，这样我们就可以说我们正在取得进展？

它被视为严肃性的证明。 如果你行动迅速，说明你雄心勃勃。 如果你很谨慎，你就会害怕。 如果你要求放慢速度思考，你就阻碍了动力。 如果你指出当前的计划具有湿纸板的所有结构完整性，那么你就是持否定态度。

这就是许多不良作品得到保护的方式。

不是因为它好、有用，甚至是半途而废，而是因为它速度快。 速度已经成为一种制度麻醉剂。

它给人一种运动的感觉，而不需要判断力的训练。

“不要混淆运动和进步。 木马一直在移动，但没有任何进展。” — 阿尔弗雷德 A. 蒙塔佩尔

每个人都会感到忙碌。 每个人都会感到紧迫。 每个人都指着机器冒出的烟雾说：“看到了吗？ 我们正在做某事。” 问题是，很多所谓的速度只是对不同名称的不耐烦。

真实的速度是存在的。 真正的速度是指当工作被理解、限制清晰、相关人员知道他们在做什么、决策足够清晰、无需不断重新诉讼即可执行时，就会发生这种情况。

这样的速度实属罕见。 大多数速度都是模糊的要求、半途而废的决定、未经检查的依赖关系、缺失的上下文，以及满屋子的人静静地希望链条中的下一个人弄清楚从未真正决定过的事情。 然后，当事情破裂时，每个人都表现得很惊讶。

当然坏了。 它是在“思考是昂贵的部分”的假设下建立的。

这在软件行业中经常出现，但软件往往只是大多数人看到残骸的地方。

同样的事情也发生在运营、管理、招聘、物流、客户服务、产品开发以及几乎所有其他人们误以为活动是进步的领域。

人们匆忙地完成了应该发生理解的部分，然后花费十倍的时间来清理后果。 原本仓促的工作被记录为“快”。 清理工作被记录为“意外”。 返工被记录为“迭代”。 这种混乱被记录为“对齐”。 可预防的失败被记录为“学习”。

这就是组织最终得到无人信任的系统、无人理解的流程、无人想要的会议、无人相信的仪表板以及成为业务承载部分的解决方法的原因。

没有人着手建造它。 他们只是不断地选择速度而不是理解力，一次一个小决定，直到整个地方变成一系列类似于生产力但没有实际生产价值的纪念碑。 然后，一些可怜的混蛋被雇用来“现代化”它，这通常意味着取代可见的混乱，同时保持原始宗教完好无损。

有趣的是，放慢速度通常并不意味着缓慢移动。 这是人们错过的部分。

放慢速度意味着拒绝跳过作品变得清晰的部分。 我们实际上想生产什么？ 谁依赖它？ 如果这个假设是错误的，会出现什么问题？ 我们已经知道什么？ 我们假装不知道什么？ 以前这个失败在哪里？ 要实现这一点，必须满足什么条件？

无聊、沉重的问题使我们的工作无法变成韦科。 但这些问题让人感觉很慢，因为它们消除了人们从运动中获得的少量多巴胺刺激。

你无法摆出姿势穿过它们。 你无法隐藏紧迫感。 你不能把对话变成 PowerPoint 并称之为进度。

你必须真正理解这项工作，这是很多人都试图避免的部分。

速度之所以有吸引力，是因为它让人们保持稍微抽象的状态。 这让他们的决策变得模糊。 它让他们避免对细节负责，直到这些细节成为别人的紧急情况。

当紧急情况到来时，速度再次成为答案。 移动得更快。 修复速度更快。 招聘速度更快。 更换速度更快。 发货更快。 同样的疾病悄然成为治愈方法。

紧迫性和仓促之间是有区别的。 当某件事很重要且时间紧迫时，紧迫感是适当的。 当人们希望采取行动来缓解情绪，而又不想承担清晰的负担时，就会出现匆忙的情况。

“慢慢来。” — 巴尔塔萨尔·葛拉西安

随着年龄的增长，我对速度这一独立美德的印象就越淡薄。 我关心工作是否能坚持下去。 我关心做这件事的人是否理解问题的本质。 我关心这个决定是否能经受住现实的考验。 我关心的是我们制造的问题是否少于我们解决的问题。

这并不需要戏剧般的缓慢。

没有人需要花费六个月的时间来编写自己的部署基础设施来证明他们是深思熟虑的。 这并不是要拖延或将每一个决定变成再次会议的借口。 这是对工作的充分尊重，第一次就做好的论点。

首先了解，其次决定，只有当你完成了适当的尽职调查后，你才可以/应该搬家。

当这些步骤颠倒过来时，账单总会到期。 有时账单是一个损坏的系统。 有时这是一支精疲力竭的团队。 有时是顾客悄悄离开。 有时，每个人都在努力解决多年的手术疤痕组织，因为没有人有耐心回去了解到底发生了什么。

速度宗教得以幸存，是因为它给了人们一个干净的借口。 这让他们说世界变化太快、市场竞争太激烈、客户要求太高、团队太小、预算太紧张、窗口即将关闭……等等等等。

有时这些事情是真的。 通常，它们只是为了掩盖这样一个事实：没有人愿意在搬家之前做更慢、更艰苦的工作来理解情况。

更好的工作通常比人们想象的更平静。 它仍然在移动。 它仍然发货。 它仍然做出决定。 但它并没有将恐慌与严重性混为一谈。 它并不把每一次停顿都视为弱点。 它并不是为了运动本身而崇拜运动。 它接受了一种非常不流行的想法，即有些事情只有在你停止催促之后才会变得更快。

这就是速度崇拜者似乎永远无法理解的部分。

你可以通过跳过思考、跳过清晰、跳过上下文和跳过责任来快速行动一段时间。 但作品会记住。 系统记住了。 人们坚持维护它记住了。

最终，现实会带来它应得的。 而现实是非常有耐心的。
